analyticalQuestion: Does the proved O(sqrt(M)) all-index ceiling describe the observed heat-weighted quartic target, and why does an ordinary unweighted Rudin--Shapiro correlation not prove the desired uniform bound?
supportedClaim: The 3,840 complete L=1 heat-weighted target values through M=2048 remain at scale 10^-3 and show no numerical square-root growth. An ordinary outer three-carry correlation divided by M grows along selected dyadic levels through M=1,048,576, so the simplex heat weight cannot be replaced by its supremum in the next uniform-bound argument. The all-index bound itself is proved in the mathematical note, not by this figure.

four full-profile maxima against one finite reference line
13 dyadic unweighted convolution diagnostics through M=1,048,576
chartContract.takeaway: The observed heat-weighted target remains small while the ordinary unweighted correlation does not supply a uniform bound; the next lemma must preserve the smooth heat weights and time ordering.
